about: Ransom's Rest (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md), the first area of the Revenant campaign: a high valley in the Reaches, closed by ridges on the north, east and south, ending on the west at the Rim over Gravewind Canyon. Coordinates are Unreal world centimeters: X is north (+), Y east (+), Z up; (the doc's plan meters: X = y * 100, Y = x * 100). Heights relative to the valley's base (Z = 0). Built by Art/Models/Terrain/RansomsRest.py; checked by Tools/terrain_check.ps1 RansomsRest. The approved map's data is Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.plan.json.
name: RansomsRest

map.about: The core square (half its side, cm) and the cell size (cm) each raster aims at: 400 m at 12.5 cm heights (the doc's fallback is 15 cm), a 4096 px macro map (about 10 cm a pixel).

macro.about: The macro maps' palette (Art/Levels/area_macro.py GRADES): golden turns the meadow's greens to late-summer gold, the doc's golden grass and ochre soil.

scatter.about: The scatter mask (Art/Levels/area_scatter.py): roadside pebbles keeps every road's surface clear of stones and lines the roads with pebbles only, so no rock or boulder stands in Main Street, the yards, on the rail bed or across a junction; steep bare keeps every stone off ground too steep to walk up (the rock past the boundary, the cliffs' faces), where it would hang on the slope.

region.about: The regional height field around the core (Art/Levels/area_region.py), in cm: the valley floor's noise and tilt (meters of rise per meter north and east) and its benches (a polygon raised or lowered by height, easing out over blend), the ridges (each from its foot: height, crest = how far behind the foot the crest is, back = the outer slope's reach, band = the cliff band at the foot; a saddle lowers the crest near a pass), the escarpment (its lip, the drop to the canyon floor, how deep the cliff kit's stacked courses reach, the far wall; calm keeps the lip from wandering where a model is fitted to it), the surround ring and the backdrop. The core's outer seamBand fades into the field; no feature may enter it.

farTrees.about: The far trees on the ring (Art/Levels/area_fartrees.py; the art session's SM_FarPine_A, SM_FarPine_B and SM_FarBroadleaf, one instanced component each, tagged Beyond): from near (cm) past the boundary to the ring's edge, off ground steeper than steep degrees, the river, the roads and the clear corridors; groves from noise, densest in the woods (density, share of pines), tree lines along the slopes, cottonwoods along the canyon's river, few on the plains; thinned where no standing spot inside the boundary (nor the lookouts: [X, Y, eye over the ground] cm) sees them; about count in all.

backdrop.about: The silhouettes past the ring (Art/Levels/area_beyond.py backdrop()): a curtain per layer, distance (cm) out, from base (or lower) up to a skyline over the bearing (0 north, 90 east). Each direction's [low, high] (cm) is the skyline's range, eased between them; relief adds low rolling swells, about that high (cm) either way per direction, wavelength (cm) apart along the circle; notches [bearing, width in degrees, depth (cm)] cut soft U gaps, a side canyon's. Mesas are the landforms standing on the range's low: [bearing, width, height] is the plain flat-topped mesa; [bearing, width, height, kind] or {azimuth, width, height, kind, side, tilt} picks mesa, butte, stepped, broken or spire (side -1 mirrors it, tilt lifts its far side). The landforms and gaps west are composed for Ransom's Point and the deck (bearing 247.5): two close together, a wide gap, the big stepped one, a spire, a broken one, the 6 km layer's peeking between; the nearest layer's relief and gaps east are for the ridge foot (bearing 85).

boundary.about: The playable boundary as approved (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.plan.json), corners [X, Y] in cm in order; open lists runs of open edges (from corner a to corner b), where a drop is part of play; blocked lists runs closed by something built (Stage Gap's mouth: the parked locomotive and the rockslide). The other edges stand at the foot of rock too steep to climb: the ridges' bands, and wherever a band stands back or fades, the rock foot makes (Art/Levels/area_boundary.py).

open.note: the Rim's lip, from where Larkspur Ridge meets it round Gravewind Point and its deck to the Mooring Ledge's south edge over the Mooring Notch

blocked.note: Stage Gap's mouth: the line runs out through it, and the parked train and the rockslide close it (step 5b)

foot.about: The rock past every other closed edge (Art/Levels/area_boundary.py): the ground stays level for setback (cm) past the line, then rises at slope (degrees) by at least height (cm) and on at back (degrees), easing into the ground behind by reach (cm). It never lowers the ground, so the ridges' bands stand as they are; it's the rule where a band stands back or fades. Tools/terrain_check.py holds the rise from the line to 5 m out over 44 degrees, its foot within 2.5 m, every 5 m along each edge.

openGround.about: The open-ground metric (Art/Levels/area_open.py): every walkable meter inside the boundary is measured to its nearest break (a building, wall, fence, outcrop or boulder group, tree stand, cliff, or a 1.5 m rise within 6 m). target is the most it should be (cm); open marks ground left open on purpose, which isn't measured (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md: the hayfields, Main Street, the crossroads at the keeper's grave and the grave's line to the bell tower).

level.about: How Tools/Unreal/build_area.py builds the level (step 5a): the map, the tag and outliner folder of everything it places, the zones scattered trees keep out of ([zone id, share of its bounding box]), the scatter's PCG graph and volume (Tools/Unreal/build_island_scatter.py RansomsRest), and how far behind the closed edges the walls stand (wallSetback, cm: at the rock's foot, which rises about 2.5 m past the line). models: a placement kind's model where this area has its own (Grandma Delia's lived-in house, SM_Farmhouse_Ransom, for the farmhouse; the clapboard SM_Cottage_Ransom and the shake-roofed SM_Barn_Ransom for the tutorial island's cottage and barn). lights: the lived-in houses' lamps and lamplit windows, brighter at dusk (AHouseLights on each one's SOCKET_Light: the lamp's candelas by day and at dusk, its reach in cm), and the empty cottages' windows left dark. props: models only the build places, on the ground at their location (x, y cm), turned by yaw and tagged Obstacle like the placements; their footprints are the layout's obstacles already, so the generator needs nothing of them (the town gate over its posts, townGateNorth and townGateSouth). smoke: the buildings whose chimneys smoke (placement keys), in a half-empty town in mourning only the lived-in ones: Delia's, Pruitt's store, Tilly's, two cottages and the waiting locomotive. cliffs: the walls varied piece by piece (varied: the cliff groups), their tops reaching 72-112% of the wall (top) and one point in ten left out (gaps), so the ring at the valley's foot isn't one even picket wall; in the Sink (lean: its pit and ramp groups) every piece leans back with the generated wall behind it (measured by traces at build time), which slopes, so no piece stands buried in the slope with only its top poking out: from the floor those read as rocks hanging off the rim. materials and swaps: the area's own instances of shared materials, worn by everything the build places: the rock (MI_RockCliff_Ransom, on the cliff kit, the outcrops and Den Rock) warmer and darker than the tutorial island's pale cream, toward the valley's ochre, with only a little dry lichen on its tops in dry country (MossAmount 0.12 in a dusty grey-ochre MossColor, on the granite too: olive-green tops read damp), and the den's own rock (MI_RockCliffDen_Ransom: its pale tint times the same warming); the terrain's and the ring's steepest faces taking the rock from 40 degrees, full by 55 (MI_RansomsRestMacro_Steep, MI_RansomsRestRingMacro_Steep: the 35-50 degree faces dominate the views, and banded ochre past 50 read bare); the dressed granite blocks with no moss (MI_RockGranite_Ransom: bright moss turned the Sink's dead floor green); the orchard's leaves (MI_LeavesApple_Ransom) olive-amber with half the trees turning gold-amber (its apples are their own slot and stay red), late summer's, as the palette asks, and the scattered oaks and birches olive-drab and gold with a third of each turning (MI_LeavesOak_Ransom, MI_LeavesBirch_Ransom: Tint, and TintVariation on VariationAmount of the trees; the scatter takes the swaps as its override materials). The Sink keeps its own looks, set by build_area_sink.py on its pieces alone (not swaps): its floor's web mats in dusty silk (MI_Web_SinkFloor) and its dressed blocks in a dusty granite with no moss beside the walls (MI_RockGranite_Sink). In the Sink (lean: its pit and ramp groups) every piece leans back with the wall behind it, from the wall's real foot, and no top ends inside the wall's rounded lip (a top that would comes down under it; the ramp's walls spread their tops under it, leanTop, and stand 50 cm out from the wall, leanProud); runs that end at Den Rock reach into it (abut). The Sink's pit wall (panels: theSink) is dressed with the narrow cliff panels in short steps along its curve, each leaning with the wall and standing 0.55 m proud of its most forward point, tops under the lip, and the seam wedge in the corner by Den Rock (build_area_panels.py). The cliff pieces under the burial deck end under its boards (under): the escarpment's top course stood through the deck's open end. The windmill alone (swapsOn) trades its teal and orange rust for weathered galvanized steel (MI_MetalWorn_Windmill: the worn metal set tinted 0xb8b5ac), as the art brief keeps loot colours off the world; the barns, well and crates keep their rust.

environment.about: The golden hour tried out on Lvl_TerrainTest (Tools/Unreal/build_area_environment.py): the sun low in the west-southwest over the canyon, haze thickest down in the canyon and glowing warm toward the sun, the planet's top down on the plains, the cloud dome past the backdrop. Tuned on Ransom's Rest at step 5a. Art note 3 (the sky): the sky's own color cancels most of the warm sun's tint, so it stays a clear blue overhead and warms only toward the sun; the haze ends at 13.5 km, between the backdrop (12 km) and the cloud dome (15 km), so neither the sky nor the clouds wear it; the haze's glow toward the sun matches the warm sky there. Art note 2 (the far band): the fog thinned to 0.003 (dusk 0.004) and the atmosphere's own haze stretched 3 times, so the backdrop's layers fade by distance, darker near and paler far, instead of melting into one pale band; M_Backdrop darkens them toward the sun to their shaded sides.

Dusk.about: The scripted dusk (step 13; the cold open and Main 6, Looter.Light Dusk), tuned on Lvl_TerrainTest: the sun 4 degrees over the horizon a little further west, warmer and dimmer, its long shadows capped at 60 m; the sky light dimmer, recaptured behind the switch; the haze cooling to a dim violet away from the sun, still glowing amber toward it; the backdrop's ranges darkened and warmed through MPC_Lighting so none shows bright at sunset; the exposure lifted a little so the fight stays readable. Art note 3 (the sky): the ozone raised to 3.5 times Earth's and the sky's color corrected, so the sky away from the sun turns twilight's blue-violet while it still burns orange to pink around the sun; the sun at 3600 K rather than 3200 K, since the ozone reddens its light too; the clouds dimmed and warmed so their lit sides glow peach against the violet.

gameplay.about: No creatures or director yet: the encounters (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md, "Encounters stay on one level of ground") are placed with their missions from step 14 on. The story's first arrival (spawnLanding) is a player start of its own beside the level's start by Ellis's grave; the depot's station carries Landing_Depot (build_area_travel.py).
